title: ALMA Discovery of a Disk around the Planetary-mass Companion SR 12 c
question: Can deep ALMA Band 7 observations detect and characterize the physical properties (flux density, dust mass, radius, and gas content) of the circumplanetary accretion disk around the wide planetary-mass companion SR 12 c?

data.sensitivity: 10 uJy beam^-1 (continuum around map center); 19 uJy beam^-1 (continuum at SR 12 AB); ~0.7 mJy beam^-1 per 1 km s^-1 (CO-free channels)

what.value: Gaia DR2 distance of 112.5 (+5.8/-5.3) pc, proper motion of SR 12 AB, and positions of SR 12 c in Gaia DR2 and EDR3

evidence.quote: The separation between AB is 0.21$''$ (cite: K11), or about 24 au given the Gaia DR2[^1] distance of $112.5^{+5.8}_{-5.3}$ pc (cite: GaiaDR2; BJ18).

This is slightly different from the positions of SR 12 c in Gaia DR2 ($16^{\mathrm{h}}27^{\mathrm{m}}19.659s$, $-24\ensuremath{^\circ}41\ensuremath{'}49.22\ensuremath{''}$; epoch J2015.5) and EDR3 ($16^{\mathrm{h}}27^{\mathrm{m}}19.658s$, $-24\ensuremath{^\circ}41\ensuremath{'}49.24\ensuremath{''}$; epoch J2016), but as demonstrated in Figure 2, after accounting for the Gaia DR2 proper motion of the host binary ($\mu_{\alpha^\ast} = -7.7\pm1.1$ mas yr$^{-1}$, $\mu_\delta = -25.3\pm0.8$ mas yr$^{-1}$), the expected position of SR 12 c at the time of our observations matches the position of this 0.88 mm source.

what.value: Accretion rate of SR 12 c (10^(-11.08+-0.40) M_sun yr^-1), spectral type L0+-1, log g = 4+-0.5, effective temperature 2600+-100 K

evidence.quote: The SED fitting in (cite: SM18) yields a spectral type of L$0\pm1$, log *g* $=4\pm0.5$, and an effective temperature of $2600\pm100$ K, so the radius of SR 12 c using the Stefan–Boltzmann law is expected to be about 1.6 $R_{\rm Jup}$.

X-shooter spectroscopy in (cite: SM18; SM19) reveals multiple hydrogen lines, in particular the prominent H$\alpha$ emission, indicating that SR 12 c is accreting at a rate of $10^{-11.08\pm0.40}~M_\ensuremath{\odot}$ yr$^{-1}$.

what.value: J-band bolometric correction and evolutionary models for SR 12 c luminosity and mass

evidence.quote: Using the Gaia DR2 distance, the *J*-band bolometric correction in (cite: Filippazzo15), and the models in (cite: Baraffe15), we find a slightly lower bolometric luminosity of log$(L/L_{\odot})=-2.95\pm0.11$ dex and a mass of $11\pm3~M_{\rm Jup}$.

what.value: 850/870 um submillimeter galaxy differential number counts

evidence.quote: We calculate the probability of the point source being a distant galaxy by fitting a power law to the 850$/$870 $\mu$m differential number counts in (cite: C14).

what.value: PDS 70 c continuum flux density (86 uJy), outer radius (1 au), and distance (112.4 pc)

evidence.quote: It is about 1.5 times brighter than the CPD around PDS 70 c (86 $\mu$Jy; (cite: B21)) given their very similar distances (112.5 pc to SR 12 and 112.4 pc to PDS 70).
We find a mean disk temperature of 29 K for the PDS 70 c disk when integrating $T(r)$ to 1 au, the disk outer radius constrained by (cite: B21).

what.value: OTS 44 accretion rate (7.6e-12 M_sun yr^-1), 1.3 mm flux density (101 uJy), spectral index (2.2), and Chamaeleon I distance (192 pc)

evidence.quote: Another planetary-mass object whose disk has been detected by ALMA is OTS 44 (2MASS J11100934$-$7632178), a free-floating $\sim$12 $M_{\rm Jup}$ object accreting at $7.6\times10^{-12}~M_\ensuremath{\odot}$ yr$^{-1}$ (cite: J13).
Its disk has a 1.3 mm flux density of 101 $\mu$Jy (cite: B17), translating to 238 $\mu$Jy at 0.88 mm assuming a spectral index of 2.2 (cite: Ribas17).

Adopting a Gaia DR2 distance of 192 pc to the Chamaeleon I star-forming region (cite: Dzib18) and assuming the same $T_{\rm mean}$ and opacity as the SR 12 c disk,[^6] we find a dust mass of 0.064 $M_\oplus$ (5.2 $M_{\rm Moon}$) with $\kappa_{\rm 1\, mm}$ and 0.295 $M_\oplus$ (24 $M_{\rm Moon}$) with $\kappa_{\rm 1\, \mu m}$.

recipe.goal: Revise bolometric luminosity, mass, and radius of SR 12 c
recipe.method: Combine Gaia DR2 distance, J-band bolometric correction, and evolutionary models for luminosity and mass; apply Stefan-Boltzmann law for radius
assumptions: Age of 2 Myr, distance of 112.5 (+5.8/-5.3) pc

recipe.goal: Measure continuum source position, flux density, and background galaxy contamination probability
recipe.method: Elliptical Gaussian fitting in the image plane and point-source visibility fitting with uvmodelfit; integrate power-law fit to 850/870 um number counts
key_parameters: Number count integration threshold of 0.1 mJy to infinity within >=20% primary-beam response and within 0.1'' from SR 12 c
assumptions: Point source model for visibility fitting; 10% flux calibration error

recipe.goal: Estimate dust disk outer radius under optically thick assumption
recipe.method: Calculate radial temperature profile T(r) following Isella et al. (2014, 2019) and integrate Planck function B_nu(T(r)) from r_in to r_out to match observed flux density
key_parameters: r_in = 1.6 R_Jup (PMC radius), D = 112.5 pc, <cos i> = 2/pi
assumptions: Optically thick continuum emission; irradiation from host binary ignored at 980 au; mean disk inclination <cos i> = 2/pi

recipe.goal: Estimate dust mass of SR 12 c, PDS 70 c, OTS 44, and SR 12 AB upper limit
recipe.method: Calculate optically thin dust mass using mean disk temperature T_mean and Hildebrand (1983) formula, and also fit a surface density profile Sigma(r) proportional to 1/r following Isella et al. (2014, 2019)
key_parameters: T_mean = 24 K for SR 12 c (integrated from 1.6 R_Jup to 5 au); T_mean = 29 K for PDS 70 c (integrated to 1 au); T_mean = 20 K for SR 12 AB
Dust opacities: kappa_1mm = 3.63 cm^2 g^-1 and kappa_1um = 0.79 cm^2 g^-1
assumptions: Surface density Sigma(r) proportional to 1/r; spectral index of 2.2 for OTS 44 to scale 1.3 mm flux to 0.88 mm

recipe.goal: Estimate gas mass, gas-to-dust ratio, and gas disk radius
recipe.method: Multiply measured accretion rate by assumed 3 Myr remaining disk lifetime to get gas mass and divide by dust mass; compare 12CO (3-2) upper limit to radiative transfer models of Rab et al. (2019)
key_parameters: Accretion rate = 10^(-11.08 +- 0.40) M_sun yr^-1; remaining lifetime = 3 Myr; CO channel rms = ~0.7 mJy beam^-1 per 1 km s^-1
assumptions: Constant accretion for 3 Myr; 12CO (3-2) emission is not absorbed by foreground clouds and CO is not heavily depleted onto grains

answer_key.quantity: SR 12 c 0.88 mm continuum flux density (uvmodelfit)

evidence.quote: The disk has a flux density of $127 \pm14~\mu$Jy and is not resolved by the $\sim$0.1$''$ beam, so the dust disk radius is likely less than 5 au and can be much smaller if the dust continuum is optically thick.
We assume a point source model in the CASA task `uvmodelfit` and obtain a flux density of $127\pm14~\mu$Jy, where the uncertainty includes a 10% flux calibration error.

answer_key.quantity: SR 12 c 0.88 mm peak flux density (image)

evidence.quote: This is consistent with the peak flux density of 126 $\mu$Jy directly measured from the image, indicating that the disk is indeed not resolved.

answer_key.quantity: ALMA positional rms accuracy

evidence.quote: For our observations, this positional rms is 10 mas.

answer_key.quantity: Probability of background galaxy within 0.1'' of SR 12 c

evidence.quote: The probability of one galaxy being within 0.1$''$ from SR 12 c is 0.02%.

answer_key.quantity: SR 12 c dust disk radius upper limit (from beam)

evidence.quote: The disk has a flux density of $127 \pm14~\mu$Jy and is not resolved by the $\sim$0.1$''$ beam, so the dust disk radius is likely less than 5 au and can be much smaller if the dust continuum is optically thick.

answer_key.quantity: SR 12 c optically thick dust disk outer radius

evidence.quote: After substituting the bolometric luminosity of SR 12 c into $T_{\rm PMC,\,irr}$ and the mass, radius, and accretion rate into $T_{\rm acc}$, we find a disk outer radius of 0.34 au ($\sim$720 $R_{\rm Jup}$), much smaller than the minimum radius that can be resolved by the beam ($\sim$5 au).

answer_key.quantity: SR 12 c mean disk temperature (integrated to 5 au)

evidence.quote: Integrating $T(r) = (T_{\rm PMC,\,irr}^4 + T^4_{\rm acc})^{0.25}$ from 1.6 $R_{\rm Jup}$ to 5 au (the upper limit of the SR 12 c disk radius), we find a mean disk temperature of $T_{\rm mean}=24$ K.

answer_key.quantity: SR 12 c optically thin dust mass (1 mm grains, T_mean = 24 K)

evidence.quote: Assuming the disk only contains 1 mm grains with an opacity of $\kappa_{\rm 1\,mm}=3.63$ cm$^2$ g$^{-1}$ (cite: Birnstiel18), we substitute $T_{\rm mean}$ and $\kappa_{\rm 1\,mm}$ into $M_{\rm dust} = \frac{F_\nu D^2}{\kappa B_\nu(T_{\rm mean})}$ (cite: H83) and find a dust mass of $0.012~M_{\oplus}$ (0.95 $M_{\rm Moon}$), two times more massive than the PDS 70 c disk, 0.006 $M_{\oplus}$ (0.47 $M_{\rm Moon}$).

answer_key.quantity: SR 12 c optically thin dust mass (1 um grains, T_mean = 24 K)

evidence.quote: If the millimeter-sized dust grains are already depleted such that only 1 $\mu$m grains remain, we find a dust mass of $0.054~M_{\oplus}$ (4.4 $M_{\rm Moon}$) assuming an opacity of 0.79 cm$^2$ g$^{-1}$ (cite: Birnstiel18), again two times higher than the PDS 70 c CPD, 0.027 $M_{\oplus}$ (2.2 $M_{\rm Moon}$).

answer_key.quantity: SR 12 c dust mass from surface density model (1 mm grains)
